advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that plants a device serial containing a well-formed queried volume id as a proper substring token, asserting the anchored regex refuses to resolve it (and, ideally, an AC4 seed variant that reverts the anchor to substring matching and shows the wrong device is returned).
evidence: user_data.sh:84-85 adds `nvme id-ctrl -v "$d" 2>/dev/null | grep -qiE '(^|[^0-9a-zA-Z])'"$vol_nodash"'([^0-9a-zA-Z]|$)'` — an anchored token match that is a distinct behavior change from the removed substring `grep -qi "$vol_nodash"`

The only resolve-path seed test drops the SHAPE guard, not the regex: `seeded = _run(host, 'resolve_ebs_device ""', drop_lines=("REFUSE-DEGENERATE-VOLUME-ID",))` (test line 272); no `drop_lines` variant removes the anchored-regex line

The host fixture plants serials `vol0aaa1111bbbb2222c`, `GOOD_SERIAL`, `vol0ccc9999dddd8888e` (test lines ~ fixture) — none is arranged so a well-formed queried id is a PROPER SUBSTRING of a longer serial token, which is the exact case the anchor exists to refuse

Named violating input: querying a well-formed id (`vol0aaa1111bbbb2222`, 17 hex after `vol`) that is a proper substring of a different device's serial `vol0aaa1111bbbb2222c` — old substring grep matches (wrong device), anchored regex refuses; no test covers it, so the anchor's contribution is regression-blind
advisory.finding: The newly introduced anchored nvme-serial match (user_data.sh:84-85, replacing the old `grep -qi "$vol_nodash"` substring test) has no test that exercises it as the sole discriminator; every truncation/degenerate case is caught first by the shape guard, so reverting the anchor to the original substring grep would keep the whole suite green.
scenarios: A refactor or accidental revert changes line 85 back to `grep -qi "$vol_nodash"`; all tests still pass because the shape guard already refuses the degenerate inputs the suite feeds it
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test where `serials/nvme2n1` holds a longer token embedding the queried well-formed id as a substring (e.g. queried `vol-0aaa1111bbbb2222c` vs a planted serial line `xvol0aaa1111bbbb2222cy`), asserting `resolve_ebs_device` does NOT return nvme2n1; optionally a seed test dropping only the anchored-regex line to prove it is load-bearing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Validate the raw volume-id argument shape (`^vol-([0-9a-f]{8}|[0-9a-f]{17})$`) before stripping dashes, so misplaced/extra dashes are refused rather than normalized into an accepted id.
evidence: infra/terraform/user_data.sh:53 `grep -qiE '^vol([0-9a-f]{8}|[0-9a-f]{17})$'` — validation runs on the already-de-dashed value, so dash placement in the raw arg is not constrained
advisory.finding: `require_well_formed_volume_id` validates the DE-DASHED string (`vol_nodash=$(echo "$1" | tr -d '-')`), so `tr -d '-'` strips dashes from anywhere in the argument, not just the canonical single `vol-` separator; an input like `v-o-l-0ddd3333eeee4444f` or `vol--0ddd...` collapses to an accepted shape and is treated as well-formed.
scenarios: An operator hand-runs the mount steps (per infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:692) and pastes a mistyped id with stray dashes; it normalizes into an accepted form and the anchored serial match then decides whether it resolves a real device.
advisory.suggested_fix: Validate `$1` directly against `^vol-([0-9a-f]{8}|[0-9a-f]{17})$` (dash included, anchored) before the `tr -d '-'` normalization, then de-dash for the serial match.
